title: EPIC: LIBS Integration into rust-daq
description:
Integrate LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy) hardware and experiments from the Python LIBS codebase into the rust-daq unified framework.

## Overview
Port the LIBS Python codebase to rust-daq, enabling unified instrument control for both RASHG (maitai) and LIBS systems.

## Hardware Inventory (NEW - different from RASHG)
1. **Andor iStar sCMOS Camera** - Gated ICCD with DDG, MCP gain (Windows SDK)
2. **Andor ATSpectrograph** - Grating control, wavelength calibration (Windows SDK)
3. **Dover Motion XYZ Stages** - High-speed 3-axis, Trigger-On-Position (C++ API, Linux support!)
4. **Spirit Laser** - Picosecond laser via CANopen protocol
5. **NI-DAQmx** - Triggering/pulse generation (Windows)

## Key Experiments to Port
- Single-shot/multi-shot spectroscopy
- Step scans (X, Y, Z, 2D grids)
- Trigger-On-Position rapid acquisition
- Delay scans (DDG timing)
- Radiance calibration

## Architecture Notes
- Dover Motion has C++ API with Linux support (no PyO3 needed!)
- Andor SDK3 requires FFI bindings via bindgen
- Spirit laser can use existing Rust CANopen crates
- Feature flag: `libs` for LIBS-specific drivers

## Documentation
- Dover Motion API: LIBS/docs/dover-motion-api/
- Original Python code: LIBS/initialization.py, LIBS/experiments.py

title: Add watchdog for orphaned RunEngine plans
notes:
## Problem
RunEngine plans can become orphaned if:
- Client disconnects mid-execution
- Network failure interrupts gRPC stream
- Panic in user-provided plan step callback

There's no automatic timeout or cleanup for stalled plans.

## Solution
Add watchdog timer to RunEngine:
- Configurable inactivity timeout (default 30s)
- Detect when no plan progress occurs
- Emit warning/error event on timeout
- Option to auto-abort stalled plans

## Implementation Notes
- Add `plan_timeout` config option to RunEngine
- Track last activity timestamp per active plan
- Spawn watchdog task that checks periodically
- Fire `PlanTimeout` event before abort

## Location
- crates/daq-experiment/src/engine.rs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Plans timeout after configurable period of inactivity
- [ ] PlanTimeout event fired before automatic abort
- [ ] Watchdog is cancellable when plan completes normally
- [ ] Unit tests for timeout behavior

title: Add Frame Pool Timeout Protection
description:
## Objective
Prevent UI stalls from crashing hardware by adding timeouts to frame pool acquisition.

## Current Problem
- FrameProducer uses pool::Loaned<FrameData> for zero-copy streaming
- If UI holds 100% of pool buffers (paused debugger, memory leak, slow processing):
  - Camera driver blocks indefinitely waiting for buffer
  - Hardware loop hangs
  - Potential SDK timeout/crash
  - No visibility into the issue

## Implementation Plan
1. Add timeout parameter to pool buffer acquisition
2. If pool empty for >1 second, drop the frame instead of blocking
3. Log warning: "Frame Dropped (Pool Empty) - consumers too slow"
4. Add metrics: pool_exhaustion_count, frames_dropped_backpressure
5. Consider adaptive behavior: reduce frame rate when pool pressure detected

## Code Location
- crates/pool/src/lib.rs (buffer acquisition)
- crates/driver-pvcam/src/acquisition.rs (frame producer loop)
- crates/driver-mock/src/mock_camera.rs (reference implementation)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timeout on buffer acquisition (configurable, default 1s)
- [ ] Frame dropped instead of blocking when pool exhausted
- [ ] Warning logged with context
- [ ] Metrics exposed for monitoring
- [ ] Camera driver never blocks indefinitely

## Testing
- Create test that holds all pool buffers
- Verify driver continues running (dropping frames)
- Verify warning logged

title: Phase 1: Re-enable cast lints as WARN
description:
## Phase 1: Visibility (No Breaking Changes)

**Goal:** Make dangerous casts visible without blocking CI

**Steps:**
1. Change Cargo.toml lines 53-57 from `allow` to `warn`
2. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets 2>&1 | grep cast_ | wc -l` to count warnings
3. Document the count and hotspot files in a comment
4. CI remains green (warnings don't fail)

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Lints changed to warn level
- [ ] Warning count documented
- [ ] CI passes

This is safe to merge immediately - provides visibility without risk.

title: Phase 2: Fix or justify all cast warnings
description:
## Phase 2: Address Each Warning

**Goal:** Resolve all cast warnings from Phase 1

**Steps:**
For each cast warning, choose one:

1. **Fix with bounds checking:**
   ```rust
   let val = u32_value.try_into().expect("value must fit in u16");
   // or
   let val = u32_value.min(u16::MAX as u32) as u16;
   ```

2. **Explicit allow with justification:**
   ```rust
   #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
   // SAFETY: PVCAM API guarantees width fits in u16 (max 4096)
   let width = frame_width as u16;
   ```

**Priority Files:**
- daq-driver-pvcam (hardware register casts)
- daq-driver-comedi (channel/range indices)
- daq-egui (UI dimensions)

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Zero cast warnings remain
- [ ] Each #[allow] has a // SAFETY comment
- [ ] No silent truncation possible
